paper_metadata.title: Quantum-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning for Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) Liquidity Management

summary: The paper proposes a hybrid QSAC framework for CBDC liquidity management using a 4-qubit, 6-layer hardware-efficient variational quantum circuit in the critic, trained for 500,000 timesteps. In simulation, QSAC achieves 12.4 bps average funding cost and 0.0% LCR breaches, compared with Classical SAC at 13.1/12.9/13.5 bps, SMPC at 12.8 bps, RMPC at 13.2 bps, and Rule-Based at 15.8 bps; the paper also reports a 0.0023 mean gradient variance in early training and IBM Nairobi-calibrated noise mitigation via ZNE.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical Soft Actor-Critic (QSAC) for CBDC liquidity management using a 4-qubit, 6-layer hardware-efficient variational quantum circuit in the critic, evaluated in a five-bank simulated liquidity network under multiple stress scenarios and compared against classical DRL and MPC baselines.

algorithm.variant: Quantum-Enhanced Soft Actor-Critic (QSAC) with hardware-efficient VQC critic

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 65-dimensional state vector fed into a hybrid critic; 4-qubit VQC used as a variational feature map/critic component
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize expected return with entropy regularization while minimizing funding cost and penalizing LCR breaches: R(st, at) = -(Funding Cost_t) - lambda1 * max(0, LCR_target - LCR_t) - lambda2 * Cost_transaction
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: penalty terms for LCR breach and transaction cost; regulatory compliance enforced through reward shaping

problem_instance.description: Multi-bank CBDC liquidity management in a network of five heterogeneous commercial banks with interbank lending, balance-sheet heterogeneity, and contagion dynamics

dataset_specification.description: five-bank simulated environment; four stress scenarios: gradual adoption, COVID flight-to-quality, SVB contagion, high-rate environment

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: simulation-based evaluation across four calibrated stress scenarios; comparison against classical SAC, SMPC, RMPC, and rule-based baselines; statistical significance reported with t-tests and confidence intervals

noise_model.noise_type: calibrated IBM hardware noise model; zero-noise extrapolation mitigation
noise_model.mitigation_details: noise model calibrated to IBM Quantum ibm_nairobi; ZNE applied by scaling circuit noise and extrapolating to zero noise

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: classical actor network with 12,784 parameters; classical preprocessing layers [64, 32] before VQC in critic
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: classical readout layers [16, 1] after VQC; SAC policy/value updates

speedup_claims.conditions: four calibrated stress scenarios; simulation only; noise-free or noise-mitigated execution
speedup_claims.caveats: Advantage is contingent on noise-free or noise-mitigated execution and is described as modest.

speedup_claims.conditions: comparison against MPC baselines in simulation
speedup_claims.caveats: The advantage narrows versus MPC; paper frames this as a modest effect.

speedup_claims.conditions: for n qubits, state space dimension scales as 2^n
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a representational-capacity argument, not an empirical speedup.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; only a 4-qubit critic circuit is studied.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 4 qubits, 6 layers, 28 quantum parameters; simulation with IBM Nairobi-calibrated noise and ZNE.
limiting_factors: Only a 4-qubit variational circuit is used
No real QPU execution is reported
Performance gains are modest and depend on noise mitigation
Classical MPC baselines are competitive and sometimes close to QSAC
The paper is a proof-of-concept hybrid simulation, not a scalable deployment

notes: Hardware type inferred as simulator_noisy because the paper reports a calibrated IBM Quantum ibm_nairobi noise model and ZNE, but no execution on a real QPU is described.
Angle encoding is inferred from the 65-dimensional state vector feeding the hybrid critic; the paper does not explicitly name an encoding method.
Speedup order is not explicitly characterized asymptotically; the paper reports empirical performance only.
Authors report QSAC at 12.4 bps versus Classical SAC at 13.1/12.9/13.5 bps, SMPC at 12.8 bps, RMPC at 13.2 bps, and Rule-Based at 15.8 bps.
The paper frames the result as 'quantum-enhanced' rather than 'quantum advantage' and states it is tested exclusively in simulation.

experiments.description: Classical baseline comparison set for the QSAC liquidity-management experiment, including Classical SAC (matched), Classical SAC (expanded), Classical SAC (standard), SMPC, RMPC, and Rule-Based policy.
